boards.title: Your First Weekend at Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University-Daytona Beach, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A conservative Saturday-to-Sunday sequence combining student spaces, recreation, aviation context, and public Daytona Beach destinations. Confirm operating conditions before setting out.

cards.title: Saturday Start: Learn the Student Union
cards.subtitle: Morning orientation point at Building 610
cards.notes: Begin at the Welcome Desk, identify dining and event spaces, and save the union as your reference point for the rest of campus.
cards.short_summary: Use the campus hub to establish your bearings before the weekend unfolds.
cards.evidence_claim: Embry-Riddle’s current campus map identifies the Mori Hosseini Student Union as Building 610 and lists its Welcome Desk, dining, Event Center, and student services.
cards.access_notes: Campus conditions and individual service schedules can vary; follow posted access instructions and carry an EagleCard if applicable.

cards.title: Saturday Morning: Locate Your Study Base
cards.subtitle: Third and fourth floors of the Student Union
cards.notes: Find the third-floor entrance, note the quiet and group-study areas, and check the library calendar before planning a longer session.
cards.short_summary: A short walkthrough now makes the library easier to use when coursework begins.
cards.evidence_claim: Hunt Library’s official page places its Daytona Beach entrance on the third floor of the Mori Hosseini Student Union and provides library floor plans.
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current operating calendar before visiting. Weekend visitors needing parking permits should follow Campus Safety instructions.

cards.entity_name: Mori Hosseini Student Union Gaming Lounge
cards.title: Saturday Midday: Try the Gaming Lounge
cards.subtitle: A casual student-space stop inside the union
cards.notes: Drop in only if the lounge is open, learn what equipment or check-in rules apply, and keep the visit flexible around scheduled campus events.
cards.short_summary: The gaming lounge offers a low-pressure way to explore student life indoors.
cards.evidence_claim: An Embry-Riddle campus-life feature identifies the gaming lounge in the Mori Hosseini Student Union as a place Daytona Beach students spend time.
cards.source_title: What's Happening on the Daytona Beach Campus?
cards.access_notes: Current lounge hours, equipment availability, and eligibility are not stated on the cited page; verify them in the Student Union.

cards.title: Saturday Afternoon: Tour the Fitness Complex
cards.subtitle: Student recreation at Building 261
cards.notes: Bring your EagleCard, ask about current facility rules, and choose an activity suited to your experience instead of assuming every area is open.
cards.short_summary: Use the first weekend to understand the campus recreation setup and entry rules.
cards.evidence_claim: Embry-Riddle states that Daytona Beach students have access to the Eagle Fitness Center and identifies the Fitness Center at 1 Aerospace Boulevard, Building 261.
cards.source_title: Fitness and Recreation | Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University
cards.access_notes: Access is for eligible Embry-Riddle students, faculty, staff, and alumni. Verify current weekend hours and bring the required university identification.

cards.title: Saturday Afternoon: Check the Campus Pool
cards.subtitle: An optional recreation stop for eligible students
cards.notes: Confirm that recreational swim is available, review posted safety rules, and pack appropriate swim gear before making this your workout stop.
cards.short_summary: A quick pool check reveals whether swimming fits your regular campus routine.
cards.evidence_claim: Embry-Riddle’s fitness page says Daytona Beach students, faculty, staff, and alumni have access to the Tine W. Davis Swimming Pool.
cards.source_title: Fitness and Recreation | Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University
cards.access_notes: Eligibility does not guarantee open swim at every time. Check the current pool schedule, supervision status, and posted facility rules.

cards.title: Saturday Evening: Walk an Archaeological Park
cards.subtitle: Lake, historical site, and wildlife habitat
cards.notes: Arrive with daylight remaining, follow the walking trail, and read the historical context while giving migratory birds plenty of space.
cards.short_summary: Close Saturday with a quiet outdoor stop grounded in Daytona Beach history.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Daytona Beach says Samuel Butts Youth Archaeological Park includes a lake, historical site, migratory-waterfowl sanctuary, walking and bicycling trail, pavilion, and fishing pier.
cards.source_title: Samuel Butts Youth Archaeological Park | Daytona Beach, FL
cards.access_notes: The city lists park hours as dawn to dusk. Leave before dusk and observe posted trail, wildlife, fishing, and weather notices.

cards.title: Sunday Morning: Pause at City Island
cards.subtitle: A waterfront park with docks and picnic space
cards.notes: Start Sunday with a waterfront walk, identify the public amenities you may reuse later, and avoid restricted dock or construction areas.
cards.short_summary: City Island provides an easygoing outdoor reset before exploring downtown.
cards.evidence_claim: Daytona Beach’s official parks brochure places City Island Park at 113 Jackie Robinson Parkway and lists picnic tables, pavilions, fishing docks, a boat dock, and outdoor volleyball.
cards.access_notes: Consult posted park and dock notices on arrival. The cited brochure does not state current daily hours or admission requirements.

cards.title: Sunday Midday: Follow the Riverfront Trail
cards.subtitle: A linear park beside the Halifax River
cards.notes: Walk a manageable section of the cushioned trail, pause at the gardens or overlook, and carry water for exposed stretches.
cards.short_summary: The esplanade connects exercise, river views, gardens, and downtown public space.
cards.evidence_claim: Daytona Beach’s 2024–2025 CRA report describes the Riverfront Esplanade as a 22.5-acre linear park with a cushioned trail, riverfront views, gardens, ponds, restrooms, and an event lawn.
cards.access_notes: Use marked public paths and observe any event, weather, maintenance, or waterfront restrictions posted during the visit.

cards.title: Sunday Afternoon: Reach the Oceanfront
cards.subtitle: Public park beside the Daytona Beach Pier
cards.notes: Use the park as the named meeting point, check beach-condition flags, and stay within guarded or clearly designated public areas.
cards.short_summary: An oceanfront park creates a clear, documentable endpoint for Sunday afternoon.
cards.evidence_claim: Daytona Beach’s official parks brochure identifies Breakers Oceanfront Park at 13 South Atlantic Avenue, beside the Daytona Beach Pier, and describes it as a 2.5-acre park.
cards.access_notes: Check current beach, pier, surf, weather, parking, and event notices. The cited brochure does not specify park hours or admission terms.

cards.entity_name: Embry-Riddle Daytona Beach Campus Map Loop
cards.title: Sunday Evening: Rehearse Your Campus Route
cards.subtitle: A self-guided loop through named academic landmarks
cards.notes: Use the current map to trace residence-to-class routes, note building numbers, and finish before lighting or weather makes navigation harder.
cards.short_summary: End the weekend by turning campus landmarks into a practical weekday route.
cards.evidence_claim: Embry-Riddle’s current interactive campus-map page is designed to locate academic buildings, the flight line, residence halls, dining, and parking across the Daytona Beach campus.
cards.source_title: Daytona Beach Campus Map | Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University
cards.access_notes: Remain on public campus paths, obey building-access restrictions, and do not enter the flight line or other controlled operational areas.

warnings: Current operating hours were not assumed where direct official pages did not state them; cards instruct students to verify schedules and posted access conditions.
Coordinates and maps URLs are null except for the supplied campus coordinate because card-level coordinates were not independently verified from direct sources.
The official 2026 museum page says the local art, science, and history museum is closed to daily public admission, so it was excluded.
